attacks.claim: The PR claims startup fails when the secret is missing or short, but the diff never constructs Settings or calls get_settings() at boot. The route resolves settings per request via Depends, so a bad secret would more likely surface as a 500 on webhook requests. No test covers the startup failure.
attacks.evidence: "startup fails if it is missing or short"; ABSENT: any eager Settings()/get_settings() call at startup, or a test asserting boot failure

attacks.claim: The fail-closed rollout has no rollback or staged mode. A misconfigured secret, a vendor format mismatch, or a host clock more than 5 minutes off would reject every delivery with a warning-level log and no metric or alert, silently dropping readings.
attacks.evidence: log.warning("plugcloud webhook rejected: %s", exc) -- ABSENT: log-only/report-only mode, rollback plan, rejection metric or alert, or a fixture captured from a real PlugCloud delivery

attacks.claim: The 5-minute staleness window turns any late vendor retry into a permanent 401. Readings sent while the instance was down could be lost on recovery. The PR does not state whether the vendor retries or re-signs with a fresh timestamp.
attacks.evidence: "rejects deliveries more than 5 minutes old or in the future"; ABSENT: vendor retry/backoff policy and whether retries are re-signed

attacks.claim: The 32-character minimum checks length only, with no entropy requirement, so a long but weak secret such as repeated characters passes startup validation.
attacks.evidence: if len(v.get_secret_value()) < 32: raise ValueError("must be at least 32 characters")

attacks.claim: The signature comparison is case-sensitive. If PlugCloud emits uppercase hex, every valid delivery would be rejected. The artifact does not specify the vendor's hex casing.
attacks.evidence: hmac.compare_digest(expected.encode(), signature.removeprefix("v1=").encode()) -- ABSENT: vendor hex casing

attacks.claim: Authenticated but malformed payloads return 422 with no log line, unlike the 401 path. Ops cannot see them, and a vendor may treat 422 as permanent and drop the batch.
attacks.evidence:
except ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="invalid payload") from None

attacks.claim: The public endpoint logs at warning level on every rejected request with no rate limit or sampling, so an attacker can flood logs and fill disk.
attacks.evidence: log.warning("plugcloud webhook rejected: %s", exc) -- ABSENT: rate limiting or log sampling
